confusion_pairs.quick: Classical: association between stimuli. Operant: consequences shape behavior.
Proactive: old interferes with new. Retroactive: new interferes with old.
Piaget emphasizes stages and self-construction; Vygotsky emphasizes social mediation and the ZPD.
Fluid: novel problem solving. Crystallized: acquired knowledge and skills.
Reliability = consistency. Validity = whether the test measures what it claims to measure.
Type I: reject a true null. Type II: fail to reject a false null.
Assimilation fits new experience into an existing schema; accommodation changes the schema.
Intrinsic: activity is rewarding in itself. Extrinsic: behavior is driven by separable outcomes.
Schizophrenia involves psychotic symptoms; schizotypal personality disorder is a pervasive interpersonal/cognitive pattern.
Negative reinforcement removes a stimulus to increase behavior; punishment decreases behavior.
